brief.description: Thick crude petroleum surface for natural oil seeps and finite underground reservoirs
brief.purpose: Make the natural oil seep and underground crude reservoir read as thick liquid from above and beside the pool.
brief.silhouette: A flat Minecraft fluid face with no container or separate geometry.
brief.bounds: One 64x64-pixel face, exported as eight stacked animation frames.
brief.materials: Near-black charcoal and black-brown petroleum with subtle umber depth and sparse broken cool gray-blue glints; no steel or ornamental detail.
brief.interfaces: Shared by surface flowing oil and finite reservoir oil; no buckets or canister acquisition from world fluid.
brief.states: A slow looping eddy animation, with fluid height and directional flow determined by Minecraft.
brief.construction: Generated high-resolution master, periodic edge blending, 64x64 downsample and eight looping warped frames.
brief.invariants: The surface clue must not replenish or count toward the finite reservoir; underground oil remains stationary and physically drained.
brief.technological_stage: Natural frontier crude before refinery processing.
brief.material_behavior: Viscous, dark, slow to traverse and slower to spread than water.
brief.signature_feature: A quiet near-black liquid body with subtle heavy movement and scattered small cool reflections.
brief.neighboring_assets: Oil Derrick timber frame, deepslate reservoir cavity, bare stone and dirt terrain.

references.role: Existing Photon industrial-scene scale and contrast only; not a model for oil shape.
User-supplied oil photograph for darkness, viscous material and sparse cool specular highlights only; do not copy composition or watermark.

generations.prompt: Create a single square, seamless tileable material texture master for the surface of crude petroleum in a Minecraft-like 64-pixel texture pack. Image fills the entire square edge-to-edge, viewed straight down, with no border, no container, no objects, no text. High-resolution deliberate pixel art with broad coherent clusters designed to survive reducing to 64×64: near-black umber base, dark warm brown transparent-looking eddies, a few restrained amber-copper reflective ribbons and broken tiny highlights. Oil should read as a thick viscous liquid, not solid stone, asphalt, dirt, water, lava, or a glossy mirror. Use organically flowing, slow-moving swirl forms; there must be a recognizable repeated flow direction that can plausibly animate by scrolling/cycling frames. Keep no single highlight larger than about one eighth of the tile, avoid high-frequency pixel noise and stark white streaks. Restrained late-19th-century industrial visual family, readable under Photon shaders and against deepslate/soil. Exact seamless edges so the texture tiles without a grid. Output one texture only.

Edit the first supplied image, a square high-resolution pixel-art texture master for crude oil. Use the second supplied oil photograph ONLY as a material/color reference, not as a composition: do not copy its watermark, bubble placement, photographic lighting, or text. The current first image has conspicuous broad luminous orange/amber swirling ribbons; remove those. Create a continuous nearly black, heavy petroleum liquid surface viewed directly from above. About 85-90% of the surface should be dark charcoal and black-brown, with very subtle muted umber movement and low contrast soft folds. Add a few sparse, small, broken cool slate-blue/gray-silver specular glints across the surface, perhaps a few tiny warm-brown hints beneath, but NO broad copper/orange ribbons, NO bright white patches, NO large bubbles, NO yellow glow, NO terrain, NO border, NO objects, NO text. Should feel deep, viscous, reflective only in a few places, quiet and menacing. Purposeful high-resolution pixel art clusters and crisp shapes designed to remain legible when later reduced to a 64-pixel Minecraft fluid tile, but do not render this master at 64 pixels. Keep the entire square filled edge-to-edge with broadly seamless periodic visual character; no obvious central focal point. Maintain one coherent material across the tile.

criteria.silhouette_scale: A full face of broad, winding liquid eddies; enough structure remains after reduction to 64 pixels.
criteria.implementable_geometry: Uses the existing Minecraft fluid surface and side geometry, so no custom mesh is required.
criteria.mechanics_clearance: No mesh or mechanical parts; fluid heights remain controlled by block states.
criteria.period_materials: Natural dark crude has restrained warm reflections and no decorative metal or magical glow.
criteria.family_consistency: The near-black oil contrasts with the existing iron refinery and timber derrick without borrowing their ornamental marks.
criteria.controls_readability: There are no controls on this material texture.
criteria.gameplay_scope: The graphic adds no acquisition or resource simulation rules.

criteria.matches_direction: The native reduction retains broad amber eddies on a dark oil body from the selected generated master.
criteria.geometry_uvs: One periodic 64-pixel fluid face with eight 64-pixel animation frames; built-in fluid geometry supplies levels and edges.
criteria.material_consistency: The same atlas is used by surface and reservoir crude fluid states.
criteria.assembly_interfaces: Liquid renderer uses the registered still and flowing atlas; no separate model interfaces.
criteria.animation_states: A looping eight-frame subpixel warp changes the eddies slowly without a hard cycle reset.
criteria.native_size_readability: Large continuous dark areas and broad warm eddies remain legible at 64 pixels.
